title: DeWanna Bonner landing spots: Three WNBA championship contenders who could add star veteran - CBS Sports
description: Bonner is leaving the Mercury with Phoenix out of playoff contention, so where could the 39-year-old land?
body:
Bonner is leaving the Mercury with Phoenix out of playoff contention, so where could the 39-year-old land?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:02 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        WNBA veteran DeWanna Bonner has agreed to a buyout with the Phoenix Mercury, giving the six-time All-Star a chance to compete for a championship in what could potentially be her last season in the league. The question now is where could the 39-year-old finish her accomplished career?Bonner already won two titles in 2009 and 2014, both with Phoenix. Besides four years with Connecticut and part of a season with the Fever, she has mostly been part of the Mercury. In her 17th WNBA season, the 6-foot-4 wing is averaging 10.6 points and 6.1 rebounds per game. She is a versatile, dynamic scorer and an elite rebounder, ranking in the top five for most career rebounds in league history.The timing of the buyout was not by chance. Monday was the deadline for player playoff eligibility from waivers. Because Bonner was waived by Monday, she is eligible to play in the playoffs with another team. Any player waived after Monday could sign with another team for the remainder of the regular season, but could not participate in the playoffs. The Mercury (13-24) have also officially been eliminated from the playoffs, so this gives Bonner a chance to go out on top if she is planning to retire after this season
"Because of the relationship we have with DeWanna, we worked out a buyout agreement that gives her the opportunity to chase a title in what could be her final postseason," said Phoenix General Manager Nick U'ren in an official statement. "DeWanna will always be part of the Mercury family, and we wish her all the best."
Here are the top three landing spots for Bonner:
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Las Vegas AcesAfter starting forward NaLyssa Smith suffered a non-contact left knee injury against Toronto on Sunday, Bonner's availability seems like perfect timing. While we don't have an update on the seriousness of Smith's injury yet, there is no doubt Bonner could help the reigning champion Aces during the last stretch of the regular season -- especially since depth has been an issue after the departure of Chennedy Carter.The fit makes a lot of sense, but there is a very big "if." Las Vegas does not currently have the cap space and would need to get a hardship exception. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Atlanta DreamThis is another team that needs the depth, as the Dream are averaging the second-fewest bench points per game (17.4) in the league this season, per Statmuse. Bonner is a versatile player with veteran leadership who would give Atlanta more options at the wing. The Dream (24-13) sit fourth in the WNBA standings, just one game behind the Aces whom they beat last week. Atlanta is a championship contender, especially with Angel Reese playing some of the best basketball of her career. Also of importance: the Dream do have the cap space to sign Bonner.
        
            
                WNBA Power Rankings: Angel Reese's career week has Dream back in title contention
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Liberty This is a tricky one because although the Liberty (23-15, sixth in the WNBA) looked talented on paper at the beginning of the season, it's questionable whether they are a serious championship contender. Perhaps Bonner could help them turn things around as the postseason approaches. 
New York does have the cap space, and it makes sense to add depth to the front court while forward Satou Sabally is away indefinitely due to lingering symptoms from a concussion.Honorable mentionsThe Dallas Wings have cap space and could use reinforcements after losing rookie star Azzi Fudd, who was one of the top defensive pieces for the team. However, they've had some rough stretches recently and are a championship longshot.The Minnesota Lynx are currently the top seed, and Bonner would give them another lengthy wing. But they do not have the cap space

title: Dana Brown out as Astros GM; owner Jim Crane to oversee baseball operations - CBS Sports
description: The Astros currently sit tied for first place in the AL West at one game under .500
body:
The Astros currently sit tied for first place in the AL West at one game under .500
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Houston Astros and general manager Dana Brown have mutually agreed to part ways, the team announced Monday morning.Owner Jim Crane will oversee baseball operations "through the transition period," according to the team. Brown's responsibilities will be divided among the assistant general managers -- Charles Cook, Gavin Dickey and Connor Huff -- and senior advisor Jeff Bagwell, the Hall of Fame first baseman who spent his entire 15-year playing career with Houston."Over the past four seasons, Dana has helped our organization win two division titles and has led our baseball front office through key scouting, draft and development efforts," Crane said in a statement. "On behalf of the Astros, I want to thank him for his commitment, energy, and contributions to our organization. We wish he and his family the best."
        
            
                Seven more MLB executives who could be on the hot seat after Astros' Dana Brown
                
                    Matt Snyder                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Brown took over the front office heading into the 2023 season, taking the helm of the defending World Series champions. The Astros won the AL West in 2023 and 2024 and advanced all the way to the ALCS in 2023. Last season, however, they missed the playoffs for the first time since 2016, and Brown entered this season as a lame duck. 
The Astros are currently tied for first place in the AL West, but sit one game under .500 at 65-66."I want to thank Jim Crane for the opportunity to serve in my first role as an MLB general manager," Brown said in a statement. "The Astros organization and the fans have welcomed me and my family, and I am grateful to have called Houston home for the past four seasons. I wish the organization well and I look forward to the future as I continue my 36-plus years in professional baseball."Manager Joe Espada, who is also working out the final year of his contract, has not had any "conversations about his future," according to The Athletic.
Brown, 59, played college ball for Seton Hall before being a 35th round draft pick and spending three years in the minors. Immediately after his playing days were concluded, he became a minor-league coach and then a scout. He worked his way up the chain for years in front offices, becoming vice president of scouting for the Braves in 2019. The Astros GM job was his first as the top decision-maker. Crane has been the Astros' owner since 2011. On his watch, the Astros became a powerhouse, making the playoffs eight straight seasons -- a run that includes seven division titles, four pennants and two World Series championships. Jeff Luhnow was the general manager from 2011-19, but was dismissed after the sign stealing scandal. James Click was the GM from 2020-22 and Brown took over after that.Now, with the playoffs still in sight, the Astros will be looking for a new lead executive.
Inside the 2026 seasonIt's been an interesting run for the Astros this year. As noted, they are tied for first place, albeit with a sub-.500 record.On the good side, Yordan Alvarez has put it all together -- and stayed healthy -- and is having an MVP campaign. He enters the last week of August leading the majors in on-base percentage, slugging percentage, OPS, OPS+ and total bases, while also leading the American League in average, home runs, RBI and walks. He's slashing .320/.436/.613 with 36 homers and 90 RBI. Pitching has been an issue. The Astros rank 25th in baseball with a 4.63 staff ERA. The rotation has actually been a disaster, as the Astros are 28th in the majors with a 5.15 ERA from starting pitchers. Their big free-agent signing was Tatsuya Imai, who has lost his spot in the rotation while sporting a 5.32 ERA. 
Curiously, the Astros added just center fielder Daulton Varsho in front of the trade deadline, when it was pretty obvious they needed rotation help.Regardless, the Astros got hot in late July -- winning 11 of 12 at one point -- and that's enough to be relevant in the AL West.

title: Ole Miss had FBI sweep for bugs after Lane Kiffin left for LSU, NIL director claims - CBS Sports
description: The paranoia was at an all-time high in Oxford after Kiffin left town
body:
The paranoia was at an all-time high in Oxford after Kiffin left town
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:31 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Paranoia inside the Ole Miss football facility following Lane Kiffin's messy departure to LSU last season was not manufactured. Walker Jones, the executive director of the Grove Collective at Ole Miss, revealed the Rebels went to extreme lengths to ensure no tampering or espionage was involved."We actually had the FBI come through and walk the building for bugs and for everything," Jones said on the Assorted Crackers podcast. "We knew kind of what was in Baton Rouge, and we knew how they operated. I remember getting on my knees and looking underneath desks and seeing if there was some sort of bug involved. Somebody was like, 'What are you doing?' and I was like, 'Trust me, you don't know this guy (Kiffin) like I do.'"That detail sounds more appropriate for a political thriller than a coaching change, but it illustrates how seriously the Rebels viewed the possibility of internal sabotage.The paranoia was real, widespread, and unlike anything the program had experienced during the modern coaching carousel. There was legitimate concern Kiffin might leave behind trusted assistants as de facto spies, using their continued access to players and staffers to help coax key pieces of the roster toward Baton Rouge.
That fear shaped nearly every decision during a volatile transition. Ole Miss officials questioned loyalties, monitored communication and tried to determine which assistants were committed to the Rebels and which remained connected to Kiffin. In the transfer portal era, where one conversation can trigger a roster exodus, even a hint of divided allegiance was treated as an immediate threat.Jones said he spent "several nights" sleeping at the Manning Center in an effort to retain most of the Rebels' roster.
        
            
                Lane Kiffin's pursuit of ex-NFL TE Dae'Quan Wright is latest example of LSU coach not caring what you think
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"What people don't realize is half the staff was going to LSU," Jones said. "We had to have two different text threads, two different staff meetings, we had to ask coaches to leave the room, we had no hall room conversations, nothing written on the grease boards in the office, because we were going to be competing against (half the staff for players)."
Kiffin's exit was never going to be clean, given his relationships inside the building and LSU's ability to pursue Ole Miss players. What followed was a Cold War atmosphere in Oxford, complete with suspected double agents, heightened security and the belief that every conversation could impact the roster.LSU would end up prying away only a couple of the Rebels' top players, like Princewill Umanmielen and TJ Dottery, but was unsuccessful in reported attempts to seize Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy. The Tigers signed this 2026 cycle's top-rated portal class to complete a roster that exceeds $40 million in payroll.LSU plays Ole Miss on Sept. 19The Tigers come to Oxford early this season in what's expected to be a rude welcome for Kiffin. 
Ole Miss fans do not hate Kiffin because he left -- they hate how he left. After building the Rebels into a national contender, Kiffin bolted for LSU during the most important stretch of the season, turning a potential championship run into a public spectacle centered on his future. The timing felt calculated, the messaging came across as disingenuous, and the fallout created the immediate fears of roster tampering, according to Jones. Ole Miss supporters believed Kiffin treated Oxford like a stepping stone after insisting the program could compete with anyone. Leaving for an SEC rival was betrayal enough. Trying to bring players and staffers with him made it personal.
While he's focused on his new job with bringing LSU another national championship, Kiffin said last month that both programs came out well."In a lot of ways, a lot of people won," Kiffin said at SEC media days. "A lot of coaches either stayed or came. They were able to keep Pete Golding as a head coach, so he became a head coach. Players got a lot of really big contracts in both places. Assistant coaches did in both places. Both are talked about a lot as premier programs heading into next year."It's hard to imagine Ole Miss supporters feeling the same.

title: Joey Porter landing spots: Possible destinations for disgruntled Steelers CB - CBS Sports
description: Porter has been holding in as he hopes to land a new contract
body:
Porter has been holding in as he hopes to land a new contract
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        While much of the talk surrounding the Steelers has been backup quarterbacks Will Howard and Drew Allar, the focus on Monday shifted to another player who has been notably absent this summer. Joey Porter Jr. has been present during Steelers' practices, but the veteran cornerback has yet to practice as he is hoping to land a new contract. Coach Mike McCarthy said that the team is at an "impasse" with Porter, who is also on the team's physically unbale to perform list after aggravating his back during the team's mobility test on the first day of training camp. Along with Porter, fellow defensive back Jalen Ramsey also missed training camp as he was dealing with a knee injury. Ramsey, who was taken off the team's PUP list on Monday, feels that it's time something got done with regard to Porter's contract. The Steelers' unofficial deadline to get something done with Porter is September 13, when they host the Falcons in Week 1.   "We need the whole secondary out there," Ramsey said, via ESPN. "They got to pay Joey Porter, and we need got some other guys that are out as well. So, the secondary has not been out there together yet, so I can't answer that for you."
At this point, it's more likely that Porter remains in Pittsburgh through 2026. But if that were to change, here's a look at some of the possible landing spots for Porter. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dallas CowboysDallas makes sense on several fronts, starting with the fact that Porter would complement what the Cowboys already have in the secondary. Porter could serve as a mentor of sorts for first-round pick Caleb Downs. The Cowboys, who have been in spending mode since trading Micah Parsons last summer, have a considerable amount of cap space and could make a move to acquire Porter if they were inclined to do so. Making this even more logical is the fact that Jerry Jones and Steelers GM Omar Khan have a history of working out significant trades. 
Speaking of Jones, the Cowboys' 83-year-old owner is desperate to end Dallas' championship drought, which is now at 31 years. That, coupled with the fact that Jones loves making splashy trades, makes this scenario even more logical. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Chicago Bears Chicago's pass defense was one of its biggest weaknesses in 2025, and based on how it currently looks, that may well be the case for 2026 unless the Bears do something soon. The Bears spent a high draft pick on safety Dillon Thieneman, but he alone won't help make up for the current injuries the unit is dealing with. Starting safety Coby Bryant (knee) and starting nickelback Kyler Gordon (calf) are currently dealing with injuries. It goes without saying that Porter's arrival in Chicago would strengthen the team's Super Bowl aspirations. Adding to the likelihood of this scenario is that Khan and Bears GM Ryan Poles have a history of making notable transactions. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Carolina Panthers The Steelers could trade Porter to a team that also has an interesting situation with one of their cornerbacks. Veteran cornerback Mike Jackson is entering the final year of a two-year, $10.5 million deal. Jackson outperformed his contract last season and is likely looking for a better deal for 2026 and beyond. In this scenario, it's possible that the two teams could swap cornerbacks. The Steelers would be getting an adequate and cheaper replacement for Porter, while the Panthers would have one of the league's best cornerback duos in Porter and Jaycee Horn, who, like Porter, is the son of a notable former NFL player. Pittsburgh would also be getting something else (likely a draft pick) in this scenario, given Porter's stature as one of the league's top young cornerbacks. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Giants The Giants' have heightened expectations this season that are likely buoyed by John Harbaugh's offseason arrival. But if New York really wants to have realistic hopes of competing in 2026, they need to strengthen a few areas of their team, which includes the secondary. Porter's addition would be a big boost for the Giants, who play in a division that includes opposing quarterbacks Jalen Hurts, Dak Prescott, and Jayden Daniels. Harbaugh, who coached against Porter the previous three seasons, knows firsthand how disruptive Porter can be for an opposing offense. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New Orleans SaintsLike the Panthers and Giants, the Saints are another NFC team that is looking to take the next step in 2026. After a slow start, the Saints enjoyed a strong finish to the 2025 season, including four straight wins under new coach Kelln Moore. 
The Saints could use a player of Porter's caliber in their secondary to increase their odds of winning what is the NFL's most wide-open division. With that in mind, it's possible that Saints veteran GM Mickey Loomis could work something out with Khan -- a New Orleans native whose first NFL job was with the Saints -- if he feels that Porter can help the Saints snap their five-year playoff drought. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Green Bay Packers Yet another NFC team with high expectations that is looking to separate itself from the pack (pun intended). The Packers showed last year that they are willing to swing big when they traded for Parsons. It's worth wondering whether Green Bay is considering a similar move now to add another notable player to its defense. Like the Steelers, the Packers are a franchise that measures itself only by championships. After falling short in the playoffs once again in 2025, the Packers are desperate to make a serious playoff push in 2026. That's why the Packers should be considered as a legitimate landing spot if Porter ends up on the trading block.

title: Marshall Manning recruiting: Peyton Manning's son makes high school debut - CBS Sports
description: Although 15-year-old freshman Marshall Manning played only two snaps in his varsity debut, Baylor coach Erik Kimr
body:
Although 15-year-old freshman Marshall Manning played only two snaps in his varsity debut, Baylor coach Erik Kimrey plans to get Peyton Manning's son game action every week to prepare him for the future.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It was only two snaps, but for Marshall Manning, it was the first real entry on what figures to be a very long recruiting résumé. The 15-year-old freshman quarterback and son of Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning made his high school debut Thursday night as Chattanooga (Tennessee) Baylor School defeated Brentwood (Tennessee) Academy 38-20 in a nationally televised game.Manning entered in the second quarter and immediately completed an 8-yard pass to Antwaun "Cornbread" Adams -- a four-star safety in the 2028 class -- for a first down.He handed the ball off on his next snap and returned to the sideline. Sadly there were no "Omaha!" audibles or line of scrimmage finger licks, but Manning did don the No. 16 his dad wore at Tennessee. 
The two plays weren't nearly enough to draw any conclusions about Manning as a prospect. His coach, Erik Kimrey, has a bigger plan for him.
"I want Marshall to play in every game this year, even if it's just two plays like that," Kimrey said. "Hopefully, it'll be a lot more, but I felt like -- we need him next year, and he needs to get ready."Even if his recruiting process is still years away from becoming serious, Manning's presence on a varsity field is going to draw attention simply because of who he is and who came before him.Marshall is the grandson of Archie Manning, the son of Peyton Manning, the nephew of Eli Manning and the cousin of Texas quarterback Arch Manning. Like Arch, he will have to navigate the reality that his last name makes him a national recruiting story long before he has had a chance to establish himself as a prospect.
Manning is part of the 2030 class, meaning he won't be eligible to sign with a college until December 2029. That's still some 1,200 days away. He will have opportunities throughout his freshman season to build a body of work. And given his last name, there will be no shortage of people watching."I believe we are going to see a lot of Marshall Manning this fall," 247Sports recruiting analyst Tom Loy said. "I expect him to get plenty of opportunities on the field to show what he can do."
Has Marshall Manning begun his recruiting process?Loy described Manning as a confident, intelligent player who can handle the moment when called upon, while noting that his physical development will be important as he gets older (Marshall is listed at 5-foot-11). "As he continues to see the field, it'll give everyone an opportunity to truly evaluate him, both from a scouting perspective and when it comes to potential scholarship offers," Loy said.Baylor is already looking toward Manning as a potential answer at quarterback in the future. Every additional snap will give college coaches more to evaluate, from his arm talent and decision-making to his athleticism and physical development.
There will inevitably be speculation about where Manning could eventually play. Tennessee and Ole Miss are obvious names given the Manning family's ties to both programs, but Loy cautioned against trying to project a recruitment that is only beginning."This is a new era of college football and high school recruiting," Loy said. "It is all about fit. This is a prospect with a long way to go in his process, as things are just beginning for the freshman. All that said, as long as he continues to grow and fill out physically, the big boys of the SEC are surely going to come calling."Thursday night was only two snaps. But for the next Manning quarterback, the evaluation has officially begun.
What stands out about Marshall Manning?Manning's recruiting process may be in its infancy, but industry evaluators are already trying to figure out what kind of quarterback he could become. They have 12 months to establish an initial ceiling and floor before the 2030 class begins to be evaluated more seriously.The comparisons to Arch Manning will be inevitable. He was the No. 1 overall prospect in the 2023 class and arrived at Texas with enormous expectations."I think the big initial takeaway from the limited reps that we have seen is that he's got to keep growing and developing physically," 247Sports director of high school scouting Andrew Ivins said. "He is not the same size as Arch. Could he be? I think so. I mean dad was 6-foot-5, but right now he looks to be under six feet."
Physical development will be one of the biggest things to watch as Manning's freshman season unfolds, but there are already other traits that have caught the attention of evaluators."After the physical stature what jumps out is the trigger," Ivins continued. "You can already tell that he's processing extremely fast and can get the ball out fast. I don't think he's got the biggest arm at this stage, but neither did Arch and he appears to be a little more creative and sudden with the feet."That's an intriguing early profile for a quarterback who has only played two varsity snaps. And Manning's environment at Baylor School could give him an opportunity to develop without having to carry the offense immediately.
Starer Keegan Croucher is the No. 10 quarterback in the 2027 class and is committed to Ole Miss. The offense also features five-star running back David Gabriel Georges, the No. 11 overall prospect in the 2027 class who is committed to Tennessee.For a 15-year-old freshman quarterback, that's a pretty good group of players to learn around. Manning doesn't need to prove he's a college quarterback yet. He just needs to keep getting on the field, keep developing and give evaluators more to work with."We, like many, are kind of in wait-and-see mode right now, but he's in the perfect situation," Ivins said.

title: Three Fantasy Football sleepers Jacob Gibbs can't stop drafting - CBS Sports
description: Jacob Gibbs is moving these sleepers up his draft boards and leaving his late-August drafts with them on his rost
body:
Jacob Gibbs is moving these sleepers up his draft boards and leaving his late-August drafts with them on his roster
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        I wrote up Jonathon Brooks in this morning's newsletter. Here's a link, if you missed that. My favorite sleepers this off-season have been Brooks, Josh Downs, and Jayden Reed. Brooks is no longer a sleeper. Downs and Reed still are! I write about them all of the time, though. You can read about those two here. So let's transition to three players the Fantasy Football community and more importantly your home league drafts are still probably sleeping on!Sleeper #1 - Jaylin Noel, WR, Houston TexansJaylin Noel was a very good prospect. In my opinion, he was one of the biggest steals of the 2025 NFL Draft. The Texans landed him in Round 4.His game translated right away as a rookie. He was a great returner. Noel also won down the field, and he won as a pre-snap motion threat on out-breaking routes. He is great tracking the ball, has reliable hands, and is a springy athlete who can create separation.According to Matt Harmon's Reception Perception charting, Noel fell in exclusive company in terms of grading out 70th percentile or better vs. man, press, and zone coverage in 2025. He's free in drafts. The Texans traded for Kayshon Boutte, but a late-August add leads to a ramp-up period to learn the scheme and get on the same page as C.J. Stroud in the passing game. 
Sleeper #2 - Jonah Coleman, RB, Denver BroncosDenver Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman is not free in drafts, but I do believe he is underrated. He's the Denver Broncos RB who I have ranked the highest. The opening schedule for the Broncos is pretty rough. The second half of the season looks nice, on paper.I expect Coleman to play a role on passing downs (and potentially in short-yardage situations) right away for the Broncos. I was extremely impressed with his college film, particularly in pass protection. The Broncos felt the same way. Sean Payton said, "That was a strong suit when you were looking at his tape -- different than the rest of the class," in reference to Coleman's pass protection.If there's an injury in the backfield, Coleman has a three-down skill set. He's ready to step into a bell-cow role in a top-half-of-the-league offense. And I really do think there's a lot to like about his tape as a runner. His rushing efficiency was up-and-down in college, and many view him as a plodder because he's a little buff boi. There were flashes of tempo, block-setting, and decent burst early in the 2025 season from Coleman, before he got banged-up and his offensive line struggled to close out the season. If he's a better rusher than many expect, Coleman might not need an injury to carve out a Fantasy-friendly role for himself in this backfield.
He's a bit more expensive than some of my favorite upside bench stashes -- Demond Claiborne, Emmett Johnson, Kaelon Black, and Adam Randall -- but I do view Coleman as worth a Round 10 draft pick if in need of bench RB upside.Sleeper #3 - Cyrus Allen, WR, Kansas City ChiefsI'm buying the Cyrus Allen hype. Why wouldn't we? He was productive in college, and his film backed it up. The ways he won feel sustainable. It wasn't schemed-up college nonsense. It wasn't picking on poor competition. He was winning routes. He was winning at the catch point. He has a good feel for space and was consistently presenting an open target vs. zone coverage.The drumbeat coming out of Chiefs training camp has been loud and consistent. Allen looked great in the first preseason game. Everything points towards this being a talented player who was overlooked in the NFL Draft. It happens every year.
Allen feels a bit buried on the depth chart (no surprise, we're talking about a rookie WR in August), but let's not pretend as if this Chiefs receiver room has any stalwarts on it. This is as inconsistent of a WR room as we are going to find in the NFL (Dolphins always excluded from this type of discussion). Any or all three of the Chiefs top receivers could miss time. Or Allen could just prove to be the best one. Check out the Rashee Rice Reception Perception profile. The Chiefs don't have a consistent separator. Or, they have not had one. Maybe they do now!

title: PL transfer storylines: Liverpool need help, Arsenal to get coveted striker? - CBS Sports
description: The new season is up and running and for some clubs it has only taken one game to be afforded a deeply concerning insight into the work
body:
The new season is up and running and for some clubs it has only taken one game to be afforded a deeply concerning insight into the work that needs doing. Fortunately for them, there are still a few days left in the transfer window in which to resolve some of those issues.Come 6 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Sept. 1, that time will run out. And in true Premier League fashion, there are already plenty of teams who look like they are going to be taking their business right down to the wire. With that in mind, here are some storylines to keep an eye on over the coming week:1. Liverpool's wing movesThough a 2-2 draw on an emotive day at St. James' Park is nothing to sniff at, Liverpool's opening game of the season was more eye-opening for the work it showed was needed on Andoni Iraola's squad than the battling spirit shown to draw 2-2 with Newcastle. The head coach himself is insistent that he does not need the sort of holding midfielder whose presence might have quelled some of the danger caused by Yoane Wissa and the fast-countering Magpies but he is likely to get a few new additions in wide areas.He needs them. Though Cody Gakpo was effective, scoring a brilliant low equalizer, Liverpool have been in talks with Tottenham over the sale of the Dutch international, who has 33 goals and 16 assists over 128 Premier League games. Those are hardly stellar numbers but Gakpo was the most senior option available to Iraola, who got the sort of performance from Rio Ngumoha that might be expected of a 17-year-old playing on his opposite flank. New signing Victor Munoz added a sparky presence down the right, drawing the penalty for their last-gasp equalizer, but he is not a natural on that side of the field either. Mohamed Salah's empty boots remain unfilled.
Yankuba Minteh looks to be the man to succeed an all-time Anfield great, though the Reds' first two offers to Brighton were rejected, a fee of around $95 million being set if Liverpool are to get their man. The 22-year-old may not have the sort of prodigious scoring record that Salah had in Serie A but perhaps if Hugo Ekitike and Alexander Isak, the former injured and the latter woefully out of form, can excel, then there will be little need for a scorer. Early in his career, Minteh's outstanding qualities look to be around getting the ball in position for others to score, even if he is not doing much of the shooting himself.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            On the opposite flank, the standoff with Paris Saint-Germain over Bradley Barcola continues. Is the 23-year-old winger worth the near $200 million that Paris Saint-Germain are said to want for him, their demands informed by the huge (and arguably overpriced) fee Chelsea paid for Morgan Rogers? Probably not, though it is a hard one to judge. In the last two seasons of Ligue 1 football, Barcola scored 25 goals and provided 11 assists. How different might they look in a competition where he is not playing for a team who are prohibitively superior to the field? In the Champions League, those numbers were five and eight at a rate of a goal involvement every 160 minutes.If that is it for Liverpool, there will be questions further back in the pitch. Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong struggled greatly when Newcastle won the ball on Sunday; both look as they did last season, wing backs from a five-man defense who are overwhelmed in a four. In midfield too, despite Iraola's insistence to the contrary, there seems to be a lot of pressure on Ryan Gravenberch. There is work to be done.
2. Aston Villa under pressureIt is barely over three months since Aston Villa's finest hour in a generation, a brilliant 3-0 win over Freiburg earning the Midlands side Europa League glory, their first European trophy in 44 years, their first major honor of any sort in 30. By the time the transfer window closes, there may be as few as five of the starting XI from that night still at Villa Park.Ezri Konsa, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers are gone. Villa would be prepared for Emiliano Martinez to follow, his replacement already secured in Japan international Zion Suzuki. Ollie Watkins may yet follow, Unai Emery offering barbed criticism of his star striker after he was missing from the matchday squad for the 4-0 loss to Brighton. Al-Hilal want to sign Watkins and the 30-year-old is understood to be keen on a move that would offer him a sizable pay rise.
        
            
                Premier League Matchday 1 panic meter: Aston Villa blitzed, Man United stumble and Liverpool need time
                
                    James Benge                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Whether a fee can be agreed with Villa remains in question, as does how Emery might build bridges with his star striker if a deal is not agreed. "You can call him and you can call his agent and he can respond," said the manager when asked if Watkins had refused to play. "He [Watkins] can only explain his answer, I can't."
Villa are not in the same position with their striker that they are with Martinez and to an extent, Rogers, whose place might well be taken by club record signing Johan Manzambi. Watkins played 11,817 minutes over the last four Premier League seasons, well over eight full games more than any other player in his position. Since Jhon Duran left in January of last year, Emery's squad has not really had a convincing backup at center forward, Tammy Abraham struggling for game time. The best option for Watkins-free going into this season might have been 17-year-old Brian Madjo, who has never played a minute in the Premier League and is injured anyway.Jean-Philippe Mateta of Crystal Palace, Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and Juventus forward Jonathan David have been linked as potential replacements for Watkins but there are other spots that need filling. With Amadou Onana out for much of the season, midfield already looked light before debutant Joao Gomes got a yellow card for violent conduct. West Ham loanee Aaron Wan-Bissaka covers some of the right back minutes that Konsa would have taken but there is nothing in their squad that does as good a job of filling the center back berth where he was superior.3. Is Bouaddi enough for Man City's midfield?One truth that Chelsea supporters could have told their Manchester City counterparts: Enzo Maresca is going to do weird things with his midfield. And that proved to be the case in their season opener, where the new boss insisted on hammering away with center back Marc Guehi (No. 6 in the graphic below) as the more advanced of a double pivot with Elliot Anderson. It's not the usual Maresca blueprint, which tends to involve jamming a right back somewhere unexpected, but it was customarily esoteric.
Manchester City's pass network in their 2-1 win over Bournemouth All the more so given that there were plenty of options in the XI that would have enabled him to construct his side differently. Rico Lewis (No. 82) is as much a midfielder as a right back. He could have moved infield with Abdukodir Khusanov (No. 45) in the right back slot to which he is accustomed. Even when substitutions and injuries afforded Maresca a chance to change things, he chose not to. That Guehi's header drew City level makes it feel like this gamble paid off. That the repurposed center back completed one more line-breaking pass in 90 minutes than Mateo Kovacic's five in 27 minutes suggests City might have benefitted from a different profile in the engine room.Maresca might argue he was not replete with options. Rodri and Tijani Reijnders have gone, Nico Gonzalez was on the bench but is expected to join Newcastle United. Ayyoub Bouaddi will soon join from Lille for $117 million, and despite his tender 18 years, it seems a matter of when, not if, he establishes himself in the team. A team that is competing on four fronts likely cannot call it a day there, even if their manager has plenty of fullbacks to stick in midfield. Chelsea's deadline for the sale of Enzo Fernandez might have passed but speculation over a move has not gone away. 4. Arsenal trim back their squadAnother summer of aggressive spending on ready-made players has to be paid for, even at a club who are tracking towards revenues that might eclipse every other English club ever. Arsenal tooled Mikel Arteta up for another push at the Champions League with big money signings, most notably Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa. Room must be made.
Partly, Arsenal's considerations are practical. The signing of seven senior players last year all but gave Arteta two players in every position, and when Guimaraes is taking the place of Christian Norgaard, 101 Premier League minutes, there may not be enough opportunities to go around, even when Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi get a breather or two.Then there are financial matters. Arsenal are not expected to be at risk of breaching UEFA's squad cost rules (SCR) if no more incomings or outgoings happen but they may not have as much breathing room as they would like. This is a club that has generated precious little in transfer income over recent years. So far this summer the sales of Leandro Trossard, Jakub Kiwior, Karl Hein and Norgaard have delivered around $55 million in sales and cost savings in the region of $27 million a year.More could go. CBS Sports revealed on Monday that Arsenal and Al-Hilal were close to an agreement for the transfer of Gabriel Martinelli for what would be a club record fee, expected to be around $70 million. Arsenal would like to move Gabriel Jesus on from the final year of a contract said to be worth nearly $18 million a year. Fabio Vieira, Reiss Nelson and Ethan Nwaneri could all depart, the latter more likely on loan given that the big money bids that had been expected have not materialized. Move all those players on and there is an estimated $45 million off the wage bill annually. For the likes of Martinelli, Nelson and Nwaneri, any transfer fee would be booked as profit too.

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            What to do with that SCR breathing room? Arsenal hoped to turn it into Vinicius Junior but that option dried up. Their focus is as much on transformative attacking talent as the sort of forward who would take Martinelli's spot on the left wing. Could Julian Alvarez be that? Arteta is a huge admirer and the Argentine is the sort of all-round center forward who suits Arsenal's system more effectively than Viktor Gyokeres. Still, prying him from Atletico Madrid would likely require Arsenal to obliterate their club record fee. Is that worth it for a striker who averaged a goal every other game in Spain, who would need convincing to settle for north London when he is dreaming of Barcelona?If not, Arsenal might have to settle for cash in their pocket and wait for the next big name to break loose.

title: 49ers owner Jed York arrested in Ohio, pleads no contest - CBS Sports
description: York was sentenced to two days in jail and ordered to pay $1,150 in fines
body:
York was sentenced to two days in jail and ordered to pay $1,150 in fines
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        San Francisco 49ers owner and CEO Jed York was arrested in East Palestine, Ohio, this weekend and pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, per WKBN. York was sentenced to two days in the Columbiana County Jail with credit for one day served and ordered to pay $1,150 in fines. Court documents obtained by KRON4 state the disorderly conduct charge was amended from engaging in prostitution. York was arrested by the local police department, which was assisting the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, at Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community off state Route 170.
The 49ers released a statement on York's arrest, via ESPN, saying: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."York was born and raised in Youngstown, not far from where he was arrested. He became CEO of the 49ers in 2008 while his parents, John and Denise York, assumed roles of co-chairmen. York's grandfather, Edward DeBartolo Sr., bought the franchise in 1977, while York's uncle, Eddie DeBartolo Jr., served as the team's owner from 1977 to 2000. 
York could be subject to discipline from the league under the personal conduct policy. According to the 49ers' official website, York currently serves on three NFL committees: Stadium, Media O&O (NFL's owned media businesses), Business Ventures, and Fan Engagement and Major Events.

        The 2026 Solheim Cup begins on Sept. 7 in Bernadus, Netherlands, where the European team will be looking to avenge a 15.5-12.5 loss to the United States two years ago in Virginia. Prior to the American victory in 2024, the Europeans had dominated the competition, retaining the cup three straight times (two wins and a tie), with the United States having not won in back-to-back events since 2015 and 2017. U.S. captain Angela Stanford will try to change that, while Anna Nordqvist will captain the European side looking to defend home soil for a third consecutive time. Korda will be joined by three other women from the top 25 in the world rankings -- Lauren Coughlin (No. 18), Auston Kim (No. 22) and Angel Yin (No. 25). 
As for Stanford's captain's picks, she chose Lindy Duncan, Meghan Khang and Rose Zhang. Duncan will be making her Solheim Cup debut at 35 years old, while Khang has dominated the team format with a 7-3-3 record in her four previous appearances. The other was Leona Maguire, who was one of the leaders on the 2021 and 2023 European squads. 
The other rookie is Lottie Woad, who has become one of the LPGA Tour's best since turning pro last year, earning an automatic qualifier spot after climbing to 6th in the world rankings. She will join Charley Hull (No. 7) as the two top 10 players in the world rankings on the European roster. Hull comes in with tons of Solheim Cup experience, as she and Carlota Ciganda will serve as the two most-experienced veterans on the squad.

Cleveland is turning to Watson now even though his contract makes it almost impossible for him to remain with the team beyond this year

        The Cleveland Browns officially have a starting quarterback in Deshaun Watson, and for some reason, they decided to give the job to a player who likely doesn't have a future with the team.Due to the way Watson's contract is structured, the Browns will almost certainly release him in March, and that just adds another bizarre layer to the team's decision to hand him the starting QB job. The Browns could have given the job to Shedeur Sanders, but instead, they gave it to someone who essentially has no future in Cleveland.The $200 million reason why Deshaun Watson will be gone after the 2026 seasonAfter the Browns traded for Watson in 2022, they gave him a five-year, $230 million contract that was fully guaranteed. Not only did the Browns make one of the worst trades in NFL history, but they followed it up by handing out one of the worst contracts ever. That's the kind of double whammy that can set your team back for the better part of a decade.Over the past four years, the Browns have restructured Watson's contract multiple times, mainly so Cleveland could kick the can down the road on his salary cap hits. However, the Browns also included a poison pill when they restructured his contract in December 2024, and the clause pretty much guarantees they will cut Watson by March 13, 2027, so be sure to mark your calendar, Browns fans.
Here's how the clause works, via former NFL agent Joel Corry, who laid out the details in February:During the restructure, Watson had two dummy/voiding years in 2027 and 2028 that were turned into real contract years with minimum salaries. Watson also has a base salary of $200 million in 2029 that's NOT guaranteed, but it becomes FULLY guaranteed if he's still on the roster by the third day of the league year in 2027. If the Browns don't want to pay the $200 million, they have to cut Watson before March 13, 2027. (This is a team that once had a trade fall through because they forgot to file the paperwork with the NFL, so hopefully someone sets an alarm for March 12 so they remember to cut Watson.)By the time next March rolls around, the Browns will have paid Watson $230 million, and you can go ahead and bet everything you own that they're going to make sure they don't have to pay him another dollar.If Watson were to somehow lead the Browns to the Super Bowl this year, the team would still be forced to cut him because there's no way they'd be able to afford to keep him with the $200 million salary becoming guaranteed in 2029. 
And that's the issue here: If Watson plays well, he has no future with the team. If he doesn't play well, he has no future with the team. Starting Sanders would have made more sense.
        
            
                Browns fans, keep booing: Todd Monken picking Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders is wrong, even if it's right
                
                    Zachary Pereles                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Although the Browns will avoid paying Watson $200 million by releasing him, they will have to take a massive $86.2 million dead cap hit, which will go down as the second-largest in NFL history. The NFL record for the largest dead cap hit was set just a few months ago when the Miami Dolphins took on a $99.2 million hit when they released Tua Tagovailoa.The Dolphins are taking on that dead cap hit over two seasons, and that's almost certainly what the Browns will do once they release Watson. The Browns will be able to designate him as a post-June 1 release, allowing them to divide the cap hit over 2027 and 2028:
2027: $34.7 million in dead cap2028: $51.5 million in dead capThe Browns' decision to acquire Watson has been a nightmare since the day it happened, but by 2028, they'll finally be able to put the entire ordeal behind them. Through four seasons, Watson has made $184 million for 19 starts, and he's gone 9-10 in those starts. Yes, that means the Browns have paid him $20.4 million per win. That's good work if you can get it.The Browns will pay Watson $46 million more in 2026, and that will likely be the last time they give him a single penny.

title: Lane Kiffin isn't worried about criticism over LSU's pursuit of Dae'Quan Wright - CBS Sports
description: Wright became the NFL's first active player to enter college football's transfer portal last week
body:
Wright became the NFL's first active player to enter college football's transfer portal last week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Lane Kiffin does not care about pearl-clutching from media members or fellow coaches. His job at LSU is to acquire talent, win football games and hunt championships, and his pursuit of Cleveland Browns tight end and former Ole Miss standout Dae'Quan Wright is another reminder that few coaches navigate college football's lawless landscape better.Call him shameless. Call him calculated. Call him a filthy recruiter. Kiffin will probably retweet the criticism and keep working.Wright's decision to enter the transfer portal after reaching the NFL would have sounded absurd not long ago. Now, amid courtroom victories, temporary restraining orders and eligibility rulings that continue to erase the sport's old boundaries, it represents another opportunity. Kiffin is not responsible for cleaning up the NCAA's mess. He is responsible for building LSU's roster, and if the rules — or a judge — allow him to pursue an NFL player, he likely sees it as negligent not to make the call."Because of the rulings, they are going to play for you or someone else," Kiffin said Monday. "We made the decision to recruit them. It's wrong to be critical of these kids. They were granted a fifth year and a judge said they were wronged."
That is the uncomfortable truth for Kiffin's critics. He is not breaking the system. He is reading it faster than everyone else.And that doesn't mean they have to like it.Lane Kiffin isn't changing; college football is"It used to be once you had an agent or once you went and did the combine," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said. "All those things qualified as you were no longer an amateur. You're a professional now, once you declare for the draft. So to let any of those players come back, fair or unfair to them, it's unfair to the sport, and I think it's unfair to the players that are on current teams for those guys to be coming back."College football's new era rewards aggression, creativity and a willingness to explore every available loophole. Kiffin has never needed permission to push the envelope. 
At LSU, with championship expectations and every resource imaginable, he is simply doing what he does best: winning the transaction."I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out a week ago; now I know," Browns coach Todd Monken said over the weekend. "I mean, shit, I didn't know. Now I know. I didn't call him back; I guess I should've."Critics see a broken system; Kiffin sees available talentOutrage has never altered Kiffin's approach. If Wright is legally permitted to return to college and the NCAA cannot stop it, Kiffin sees an available player who could improve LSU's roster. Nothing more.
Recruiting a player from his former program after that player already reached the NFL feels especially brazen, even by Kiffin's standards. It also reinforces every negative perception attached to his Ole Miss exit.Still, Kiffin's responsibility is to win at LSU, not satisfy a national morality test. In this era, restraint earns applause. Aggression acquires talent — and Kiffin knows that, not that he cares about outside opinion."NFL players should not be allowed to go back to play college football.  It's gross negligence," former Heisman winner Robert Griffin III wrote on social media. "It's a disservice to the current college players on any roster.  Any coach or school who allows it should be ashamed of themselves."
And Wright's not the only former college player the Tigers are looking to add before the start of the 2026 season.LSU embracing the eligibility chaosLSU also recently landed a commitment from former Notre Dame defensive end Junior Tuihalamaka, who made seven starts over four seasons with the Fighting Irish. Tuihalamaka was granted another season of eligibility as part of the Louisiana court ruling for Class of 2022 athletes.Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman wanted no part of an unexpected late addition."For us at Notre Dame, it's just too late [with] the graduate admissions process, and I don't think it would put a person in a good situation this late -- school starts on Monday -- to have success in the classroom and on the field, so that's been our stance on it," Freeman said Friday. "Our admissions has already done their admissions and cycles. That's where the university and the athletic program stand right now."
Kiffin has never cared about his naysayers, especially after messy exits at Tennessee and Ole Miss. And he certainly is not going to start now because college football's latest eligibility twist has people screaming that the sport has become a joke.The process is slimy, and many are calling the sport broken, but Kiffin has heard worse throughout a career spent testing boundaries and irritating traditionalists. He has repeatedly made clear that national perception does not drive his decisions.Kiffin's critics are concerned about what college football has become. LSU's coach is focused on winning within it. In this no-holds-barred era, yelling at your smartphone does not secure championships. Talent does.

title: LSU expected to add ex-Ole Miss star DT Zxavian Harris after NFL stint - CBS Sports
description: Lane Kiffin hasn't been shy about bringing NFL rookies back into the fold, as another former Ole Miss star is exp
body:
Lane Kiffin hasn't been shy about bringing NFL rookies back into the fold, as another former Ole Miss star is expected to join LSU
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It's not often that teams can add a standout veteran to their roster less than two weeks before the start of the season, but that's exactly what LSU has done twice in the last week. Sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz that former Ole Miss star defensive lineman Zxavian Harris is expected to land with the Tigers after a brief stint with the New Orleans Saints.Harris is taking advantage of a recent Louisiana ruling, under which athletes from the Class of 2022 have received temporary restraining orders to gain a fifth year of eligibility. LSU has already made plans to add tight end Dae'Quan Wright, who seems destined for a return to college football after being waived by the Cleveland Browns.Most recently, Harris was in training camp with the Saints after going undrafted in 2026. The Saints waived Harris on Aug. 8, and he hasn't landed with another NFL team, so it is expected that he will reunite with his former head coach in Baton Rouge.
        
            
                Lane Kiffin's pursuit of ex-NFL TE Dae'Quan Wright is latest example of LSU coach not caring what you think
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
A four-star recruit in the 2022 signing class, Harris really broke out as a senior last fall. He was a key cog in the Rebels' defense -- wreaking havoc in the middle of the line to the tune of 58 tackles, 9.0 tackles for loss and 3.0 sacks. That was enough to get Harris invited to the NFL Scouting Combine in Indianapolis.
Throughout his college career, Harris has appeared in 52 games, and he's accumulated 123 tackles, 17.5 tackles for loss and 5.5 sacks. Interior defensive line was going to be a question mark for LSU in 2026, but they may have just found a big answer with Harris.LSU addresses a big needThroughout the offseason, LSU was viewed as a legitimate College Football Playoff contender, mainly because the Tigers boast what might be the most expensive roster in the sport.Kiffin and his staff have spared no expense in hopes of an instant turnaround, but that doesn't mean the roster is flawless. Prior to the addition of Harris, there were some questions in the middle of the defensive line. The Tigers return just 31% of their snaps on the defensive line from last year, which ranks 79th in the country.
Freshmen Deuce Geralds and Richard Anderson -- both highly-touted players -- were expected to factor heavily into that rotation. Talented as they may be, leaning on a freshmen in the trenches can be a gamble in the SEC.Coming out of spring practice, Blake Ruffino of 247Sports told the "Cover 3 Podcast" that the LSU defensive line was a big question mark after watching it get pushed around by the offensive line at times."It gets to a point where, those last two weeks, it was at will," Ruffino said. "I do worry about that defensive line. Now, [five-star defensive lineman] Lamar Brown wasn't there, but my same thought is, 'Are you about to start three true freshmen in the interior of that defensive line?' Yes, it is a concern for me."The Tigers also need a lot from transfers Malik Blocton (Auburn) and Stephiylan Green (Clemson). Both had experience from their previous spots, but neither player posted eye-popping production.
Now, LSU has proven talent and experience at the defensive tackle position with Harris. The Tigers' depth at that spot now looks much more formidable, which is good because they're playing three of Blake Brockermeyer's top 10 offensive lines this fall.Have Harris and Kiffin mended fences?When Kiffin left Oxford for Baton Rouge before the College Football Playoff, he wasn't the most popular man in the Ole Miss locker room. You can certainly count Harris among the players who didn't appreciate the way Kiffin handled things.At the time, Harris told Chris Low that Kiffin taking the LSU job was "like a slap in the face and then a backhand. We took that personally."
Prior to the Rebels' Fiesta Bowl loss to Miami, there was speculation that Kiffin was trying to join the broadcast, but he ultimately attended an LSU women's basketball game. Harris didn't shy away from blasting Kiffin for attempting to steal the team's limelight after jumping ship."That's what Kiffin tried to do," Harris told Low. "He tried to be a damn announcer … trying to be a troll. We were going to troll him. We got something for him. He was just trying to steal our shine. That's all he tried to do. That's all he's been trying to do, is steal our shine."Apparently, that's all water under the bridge with Harris and Kiffin set to join forces yet again. Another payday and the chance to win a national championship can have that effect on players and coaches.
In the world of modern college football, it's probably best not to burn any bridges because things can change very quickly in an unpredictable landscape.

title: Kayshon Boutte trade grades: Texans fleece Patriots for WR - CBS Sports
description: New England strengthened a potential future playoff foe while getting very little in return
body:
New England strengthened a potential future playoff foe while getting very little in return
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A day after Mike Vrabel lamented about the state of his roster, the Patriots did something about it. New England traded receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Texans in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick, according to The Ringer. It will be a seventh-round pick, ESPN reports.Boutte, 24, spent his first three NFL seasons with the Patriots, who selected him in the sixth round of the 2023 draft. After catching just two passes during his rookie season, Boutte developed a bigger role in the Patriots' offense each of the past two seasons. He set career-highs with 43 receptions and 589 yards in 2024 and caught a career-high six touchdowns in 2025. 
Like Boutte, Reed was also the 187th overall pick in his respective draft. As a rookie last season, Reed made one regular-season start while appearing in seven games. He finished the regular season with 14 tackles and a fumble recovery. Reed started in each of Houston's two playoff games and had two tackles during Houston's season-ending loss to New England in the divisional round of the playoffs. Who won the trade? Let's find out. Patriots: D-Rumblings already existed that Boutte would ultimately be traded. With Boutte entering his final year under contract, the Patriots deserve a little credit for getting something in return for him in the form of draft capital and a player who can help them in 2026. 
That being said, it's surprising that the Patriots couldn't get more for Boutte, an emerging receiver who is still playing on his rookie contract. This just gives off a vibe that the Patriots simply wanted to get this done and move on. As noted above, it was less than 48 hours ago when Vrabel expressed concern for his team's lack of depth. And while the Patriots strengthened their secondary by getting Reed (who, like Boutte, is a player who should be on the rise), they weakened their depth at receiver by parting ways with Boutte. Making this trade even worse is that the Patriots traded Boutte to an AFC competitor (the only worse move would have been trading him to division rival Buffalo). Instead of sending him to the NFC, the Patriots dealt Boutte to a team they may very well face in the 2026 playoffs. 
Texans: AHouston deserves a ton of credit for quickly and emphatically addressing their need at receiver after Jayden Higgins went down with a season-ending ACL injury. After Higgins went down, the Texans reportedly placed a call to New England about Boutte and another to Baltimore regarding Rashod Bateman. They reportedly weren't interested in a reunion with DeAndre Hopkins, who recently became the assistant receivers coach at Georgia Tech. Given Bateman's legal issues, Boutte became the clear-cut option for Houston, who ultimately pulled off a very favorable deal with the Patriots. Boutte will now fill Higgins' spot while joining a receiving corps that also includes Nick Collins and Jaylin Noel. His arrival should also aid C.J. Stroud, the Texans' former Pro Bowl quarterback, who is hoping to return to form that saw him win Offensive Rookie of the Year back in 2023. 
Higgins' injury could have been a big blow for Houston, which is trying to get beyond the divisional round of the AFC playoffs this year after losing in that round in each of the past three seasons. The trade for Boutte has put them back on track.

title: Victory Vaka joins Middle Tennessee after NCAA fight funded by Lil Wayne - CBS Sports
description: Vaka lost his scholarship at Western Kentucky while grieving his mother's death, but thanks to a legal challenge
body:
Vaka lost his scholarship at Western Kentucky while grieving his mother's death, but thanks to a legal challenge funded by rapper Lil Wayne, he has a new home
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Less than a week after being granted an injunction against the NCAA that prevents it from enforcing its transfer rules, former Western Kentucky defensive tackle Victory Vaka signed with Middle Tennessee on Monday. Vaka filed a lawsuit on Aug. 5 against the NCAA, suing for the ability to transfer after the Hilltoppers non-renewed his scholarship. He entered the portal on Aug. 20 and signed with Middle Tennessee five days later. The Blue Raiders open their season on Sept. 5 against Murray State. Vaka is eligible to play for Middle Tennessee immediately. 
        
            
                Class of 2022 athletes lose NCAA eligibility again with more chaos coming for college football, basketball
                
                    Chris Hummer                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Vaka, a redshirt senior who transferred in from Texas Southern, flew home to California in early April to grieve his mom's death. Vaka told CBS Sports he always planned to return to Western Kentucky for the 2026 season. Nine days before his mom's funeral in May, he received a call from an assistant strength coach. Vaka said the coach provided him with a summer workout plan and told Vaka he was expected back in June.
A few weeks later, on May 27, the Hilltoppers informed Vaka they were canceling his scholarship due to his failure to report with the rest of his team. That designation of a "failure to report" prevented Vaka from entering the transfer portal under the NCAA's aid-and-reduction-or-cancellation exception.Vaka was set to graduate in the fall. He had one remaining year of eligibility remaining. But with no ability to transfer, Vaka was left with no way to play his final season.Vaka's story drew national attention after CBS Sports wrote about it in July.That includes rapper Lil Wayne, who paid for Vaka's legal fees after hearing about his story.
"Fabian Marasciullo, his manager, reached out to me saying the story touched Wayne and he wanted to help in any way possible," Vaka's agent, Jaykwon Jefferson, told CBS Sports. Wayne paid for the costs associated with hiring college sports attorney Darren Heitner and also flew Vaka and his brother out to his concert on Aug. 1 to meet him. Jefferson called the financial assistance "a major lifesaver." The NCAA and Heitner were in talks to settle the case out of court, but that fell apart in recent weeks, leading to Vaka's lawsuit. 
The 6-foot-3, 335-pound DT is a journeyman in college football terms. He's played for four schools and said he hoped Western Kentucky would be his last.Looking back at the situation, Vaka told CBS Sports in July he could have communicated better. Other than Western Kentucky flying Vaka back to campus in mid-April and his call with the strength coach, the two sides had no communication between Vaka's mom's death and the staff asking him to report in late May.Vaka said he told the staff at the time that he thought he could return in June, but offered to return sooner to avoid being removed from the roster.
Western Kentucky did eventually help Vaka file a legislative relief waiver, but that process puts the Hilltoppers in a situation where they basically had to file a waiver against themselves, per CCHA Law partner Paia LaPalombara, because NCAA rules only allow schools to cancel scholarships under limited exceptions."This puts institutions (between) a rock and a hard place -- they may want to support a (student-athlete) getting the additional 30-day window, but doing so also means that they're admitting to their own Level III violation by impermissibly removing the (student-athlete's) aid," LaPalombara said via text."WKU may have actually put forward a good-faith waiver request to the NCAA to allow the (student-athlete) to enter the portal, as they don't want the (student-athlete) to stay at WKU but also can't (or don't want to) admit to a violation that they impermissibly removed the SA's aid."
Vaka's case illustrates one of the gaps in the NCAA's current system.Western Kentucky moved on from him months after the transfer portal closed. By classifying his departure as a disciplinary matter, the school prevented him from using the NCAA's aid-cancellation exception.
